rule: History is not rewritten. The prior proof is preserved byte-for-byte beside this record; the live proof was REGENERATED by re-running the generator, never edited.

superseded.still_quotable_as: a preserved historical result under the WITHDRAWN identity contract. It may not be used as the left-hand side of an identity comparison, because the contract its ids were computed under no longer exists.

why_the_identity_contract_changed.defect: seal._code_commit() appended a COUNT of the lines of `git status --porcelain` to the commit sha. The sealing path's own outputs change that count, so a run's identity was a function of its own side effects. Independently found by WS01, WS18 (F3) and WS19.
why_the_identity_contract_changed.second_failure: A count identifies nothing. Two working trees with the same NUMBER of dirty paths produce the same string, so an edited layers.py and an unrelated scratch note were indistinguishable in the sealed bytes.
why_the_identity_contract_changed.ws19_finding: working-tree state, interpreter version and library versions were NOT_RECOVERABLE from the sealed bytes of every run tested.
why_the_identity_contract_changed.repair: nfl/identity/code_identity.py separates six identities -- A committed source, B dirty source CONTENT, C runtime, D generated artifact state, E predictive candidate, F execution -- and holds one invariant: a run must not change its own identity by writing its own outputs. D is excluded from A, B and C by a declared, versioned, hashed scope.
why_the_identity_contract_changed.why_regeneration_was_unavoidable: code_commit sits inside the sealed body and inside artifact_id's REQUIRED field list, so every run-identity hash in the proof necessarily moves. The old ids were a function of a file count; they cannot be carried forward.

what_this_proof_caught_that_the_test_sui.finding: The FIRST version of this repair kept the demoted whole-tree count inside the code_identity block as a recorded-not-hashed diagnostic -- outside the digest, outside code_version, outside ExecutionIdentity, and therefore outside identity_fingerprint and artifact_id. The block is nevertheless written into the artifact, and the artifact minus two keys IS the sealed payload, so the count reached seal_payload_sha256 and forecast_id.
what_this_proof_caught_that_the_test_sui.generalised_rule: Nothing that reads generated artifact state (D) may enter the sealed body, whether or not it is hashed into the fingerprint, because the body is hashed into an identity of its own.
what_this_proof_caught_that_the_test_sui.fix: the count is now Outcome evidence only (n_dirty_tree_entries_observed); nfl/tests/test_execution_identity.py section A now compares the WHOLE canonicalised identity block, and that check was verified load-bearing by re-adding the withdrawn field in memory and confirming it fails.

not_moved.statement: No draw changed. Nothing in this repair is on a path that produces a number.

side_effects_of_regenerating.Q9_SHADOW_DRYRUN_SEAL_LEDGER.jsonl: the dry-run seal ledger is append-only and the proof seals four forecasts, so regeneration appended rows to it. It grew from 12 committed rows to 25 rows; part of that growth is the pre-existing 2026-09-12 work and part is these runs. No row was edited or removed.
side_effects_of_regenerating.note: this file is one of the seven pre-existing modified files in WAVE0_BASELINE. WS-E appended to it by running the generator; WS-E did not edit it.
